scenes.author: Rickey Vincent
scenes.desc: Los Creators de Long Beach y Compton, «descubiertos» por Eric Burdon, que les puso delante al armonicista danés Lee Oskar: la guitarra escueta de Howard Scott, los teclados afrolatinos de Lonnie Jordan, el bajo de B. B. Dickerson, la batería de Charles Miller, la percusión de Papa Dee Allen y el saxo de Harold Brown. Desde All Day Music (1971) arrasaron con «Slippin’ into Darkness», «The Cisco Kid», «Low Rider» y «Why Can’t We Be Friends?»: la vida en el paisaje urbano sombrío de Los Ángeles (como N.W.A. veinte años después), un ritmo abierto y terroso y el foco de la influencia latina en el funk, himnos de la cultura chicana del Suroeste. Fueron la banda con la que Hendrix tocó por última vez.

podcast.title: Inspiration for "Why Can't We Be Friends"
podcast.body: Harold Brown, drummer for War, conceived the idea for the song "Why Can't We Be Friends" while traveling in Japan in the early 1970s. He observed universal human connections, noting that despite superficial differences, people are "more alike inside than we are on the outside." "We're all connected by language, he said, and by our food and by our culture. Most races don't know why they are racist, but you pick them up and take them over and drop them in a country like India or Pakistan and guess what? Why Can't We Be Friends? Because all of the sudden you find out we're more alike inside than we are on the outside."
